verdict.rationale: Statsig's docs say feature gates toggle behavior 'in real time without deploying new code' and describe an emergency disable switch that 'immediately' turns off a code branch in production, so the kill-switch capability is first-party. The pack never explains how changes reach connected SDKs (streaming vs. polling, update intervals, propagation latency), and SDKs evaluate locally from cached definitions after initialization, so the 'in seconds' guarantee is unproven. Missing for 10: documented streaming or polling propagation mechanism, stated propagation latency or polling interval, hands-on or independent corroboration that a kill switch reaches live SDKs within seconds.

support.subject: As a developer, flag changes propagate to connected SDKs in seconds via streaming or fast polling — a kill switch actually kills
